title: Linear independence of positive indecomposable roots
statement: Let $I$ be a finite set, and let $M,N$ be additive abelian groups in a perfect $\mathbf Z$-bilinear pairing $\langle-,-\rangle:M\times N\to\mathbf Z$ (the induced maps to the integer duals are isomorphisms). Suppose $\alpha:I\hookrightarrow M$ and $\beta:I\hookrightarrow N$ are injections with $\langle\alpha_i,\beta_i\rangle=2$. For each $i$ suppose there is a permutation $\sigma_i$ of $I$ such that $$\alpha_{\sigma_i(j)}=\alpha_j-\langle\alpha_j,\beta_i\rangle\alpha_i,\qquad\beta_{\sigma_i(j)}=\beta_j-\langle\alpha_i,\beta_j\rangle\beta_i.$$ These data are a crystallographic root pairing over $\mathbf Z$, as in Mathlib `RootPairing`. Let $f:M\to\mathbf Z$ be additive with $f(\alpha_i)\ne0$ for every $i$. Let $D\subseteq I$ consist of those $i$ with $f(\alpha_i)>0$ for which there do not exist $j,k\in I$ with $f(\alpha_j),f(\alpha_k)>0$ and $\alpha_i=\alpha_j+\alpha_k$. Then $(\alpha_i)_{i\in D}$ is linearly independent over $\mathbf Z$: a finite integer linear combination is zero only when every coefficient is zero. Equivalently it is a basis [def-weil-pbc-free-module] of its integer span [def-weil-submodule-span]. This includes $I=\varnothing$.
